title: Calendar Emoji (📅): Copy & Paste, Codepoint & Why It Always Shows July 17
meta_description: The calendar emoji 📅 (U+1F4C5) — codepoint, how to type it, and the real reason its date is frozen on July 17 on Apple, Samsung, Google, and most other platforms.
hero_tagline: The calendar page 📅 — codepoint, alt-input shortcuts, and the specific Apple history behind why its date is frozen on July 17 almost everywhere. Click any symbol to copy it instantly.
intro: 📅 CALENDAR (U+1F4C5) is Unicode's shorthand for dates, deadlines, and scheduling — a torn calendar page pinned at the top. Look closely on most platforms and the date on it never changes: it's fixed at July 17, a design choice that traces back to a specific Apple product announcement and later became the reason an entire unofficial holiday exists. This page identifies the glyph itself — meaning, codepoint, and how to type it — then covers the July 17 backstory in full, including the platforms that don't follow it.
